messages:
Aisha K.: paging — increased 5xx/timeout rate for inference in az1a, started ~9:02 UTC. metric spike on token latency and request errors. incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: infra.net.high_latency (sev=2) — see runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/az-network-degrade
Miguel R.: seeing packet loss counters on host NICs + resolver latency. some nodes report `kvcache miss storm` and model loads spike around same time
Riley (SRE): confirmed. traceroute shows path hiccups to the AZ resolver IPs, DNS lookup 200-400ms. backend service retries pile up -> connection timeouts to runtime.
Jun Park: impact: hosted API region az1a ~ 12% p50 token latency increase, 6% of requests 502/504s, Dedicated customers in that AZ seeing higher tail latencies and occasional model-load failures
Sam (Platform): any cross-AZ fallback in flight? routing rules should failover to az1b/az2a for new sessions but sticky sessions keep many requests pinned to faulty nodes
Elena (Support): CS pinged two Dedicated customers on sustained errors, they reported errors in user-facing features and some queued retries. prepping customer-facing note if we need postmortem
Riley (SRE): mitigation plan attempt 1: reconfigure route53 resolver policy to prefer global resolvers and lower TTL to 30s for the next 10m. executing now (will post command).
Miguel R.: agree, also recommend disabling session stickiness for 5m to let clients re-resolve and land on healthy AZs
Riley (SRE): executing: ```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"resolver.local","Type":"A","TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.11.12.13"}]}}]}'```
incident-bot: runbook step 3: if DNS latency persists, move inference traffic via traffic-manager to cross-region pool.
Aisha K.: starting traffic-manager partial reroute to eu-west-1 for non-compliant routes (10% pilot) — observe latency and error rate.
Sam (Platform): started reroute job id tm-8421 — pilot at 10% for new sessions only. older sticky sessions unaffected.
Miguel R.: spinning up 8 small g5 instances in az1b and az2a and pre-warming kvcache to reduce cold-loads. launching with image `inference-runtime-prod:v4`
Jun Park: can we reduce model load concurrency in az1a to relieve KV pressure? throttle to 60% for 10m
Riley (SRE): applied concurrency throttle on az1a routing group: `--max-concurrency=0.6` — watching for reduced errors
Elena (Support): updating customers: short note drafted, will send staged message if we cross 15% error threshold
Miguel R.: logs show kvcache eviction storm correlated with DNS lookup failures — clients retried aggressively and invalidated cache on soft errors. added short-term debounce on retry logic at edge (30s)
Riley (SRE): after route53 upsert and throttle, seeing 40% drop in 5xxs from az1a within 3m. token latency p95 still elevated but trending down.
incident-bot: escalation checklist: page network infra if NIC counters > 5000 errs/min. Riley acknowledged and will ping network team
Riley (SRE): paging network infra now — `@network-team` please advise on resolver cluster health in az1a, NIC error surge across hypervisors seen.
Miguel R.: also tracked control-plane heartbeat jitter to scheduler in az1a — some allocation delays causing model cold loads. coordinating with control-plane to bump heartbeat backoff settings
Jun Park: can we enable fallback model variant (smaller) for affected customers to reduce load? toggle now for non-enterprise customers
Sam (Platform): toggled fallback for free-tier and standard-tier customers to `gpt-lite-quant` for new requests. enterprise/Dedicated still pinned unless we explicitly reroute
Aisha K.: on-call handoff in 30m — Riley will take leader for next shift, I'll hand over context in 20m.
Riley (SRE): taking lead at handoff. current state: errors down 55% vs peak, traffic-manager pilot stable, additional az instances pre-warmed, route53 TTL lowered. continuing to monitor for recurrence.
Elena (Support): opening internal incident update doc and CS playbook — will post link in #incidents-updates when ready
Miguel R.: next steps: 1) network-team root cause on resolver cluster, 2) validate control-plane heartbeat fixes, 3) consider permanent resolver failover policy if this repeats, 4) post-incident customer comms
Riley (SRE): thumbs up. if error rate stays <3% for 15m we'll transition to monitoring-only.
incident-bot: Incident routed to P1 (mitigated) — timeline and artifacts required in incident doc.
Aisha K.: handing off to Riley now. I'll be available for escalation. :thumbsup:
Riley (SRE): copy — thanks all. continuing watch.
